h1: The 5 Best Magnetic Monitor Privacy Screens, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Magnetic Monitor Privacy Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 magnetic privacy screens for 24 and 27 inch monitors, scored on mounting design, frameless fit, pack size and ease of removal.
summary: The GUDTEKE 2-pack is the best magnetic privacy screen for a typical dual-monitor desk, giving two 24 inch, 16:9 filters that hang and come off magnetically. The JEAPKA 2-pack is a close alternative, the JEAPKA hidden design is the answer for frameless monitors, and the JEEETINTX is the one for a 27 inch screen.
intro: Magnetic privacy screens solve a real annoyance, which is that standard filters stick on with adhesive or tabs and leave residue or bent edges the moment you remove them. A magnetic mount lets you put the filter on in the morning and take it off for a presentation without a fight. The thing that goes wrong is the magnet's anchor: the filter holds to something on the monitor, and if your bezel is thin or non-existent, there may be nothing for it to hold on to.

So the first question for this category is what your monitor's edge looks like. We ranked five magnetic filters by how they mount, which sizes they fit, whether they are sold singly or in pairs and whether they work with frameless displays. We reviewed the listings, which give size, aspect ratio and mounting style but little about viewing angle or brightness loss, so we do not quote those. One non-magnetic hanging filter from the original pool was left out.

products.name: GUDTEKE 2Pack Magnetic 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor
products.verdict: Two magnetic, hanging 24 inch, 16:9 filters for a dual-monitor desk.
products.description:
The GUDTEKE pack contains two magnetic hanging privacy screens for 24 inch, 16:9 monitors. The pair is priced at $50 to $100.

It wins because a pair is the sensible unit for most desks, and the 24 inch, 16:9 size is the most common monitor format in offices. A hanging magnetic design means the filter sits on the front of the screen and clings in place, rather than being glued, so you can lift it off without wrecking the screen or the filter. That is the reason to buy magnetic over adhesive. The listing gives no viewing angle, so expect the usual trade-off of a dimmer picture.

Buy it for two 24 inch monitors on a shared or public-facing desk. Check that your bezel is wide enough for the magnets to grip.
pros: Two filters for a dual setup
No adhesive residue on the bezel
products.idealFor: Buyers with a dual-monitor desk who want magnetic mounting on both screens.
products.skipIf: Your monitors have no bezel or are not 24 inch.

products.name: JEAPKA 2 Pack Magnetic 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for Monitor
products.verdict: A second magnetic hanging pair at the same size and price, from a different seller.
products.description:
The JEAPKA is a pair of magnetic, hanging 24 inch, 16:9 privacy screens. Budget $50 to $100 for the pair.

Second place makes sense because it is almost interchangeable with the GUDTEKE on paper. Both offer the same size, aspect ratio, mounting and pack size in the same price band. The edge goes to the GUDTEKE because it targets dual-monitor desks, while this listing says little about the application. If your first choice is out of stock or you prefer this seller, there is no loss in choosing it.

Choose it as a like-for-like substitute for 24 inch screens. Compare return terms before you buy, since fit on your bezel is the main risk.
pros: Pair of filters in the pack
Same price band as the leader
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a like-for-like second choice in a 24 inch magnetic pair.

products.name: JEAPKA 2 Pack Hidden Design Magnetic Computer Privacy Screen, Frameless-Compatible
products.verdict: A hidden magnetic mount designed for frameless monitors, in a 24 inch pair.
products.description:
This JEAPKA pack has two 24 inch, 16:9 privacy screens with a hidden magnetic design that the listing calls frameless-compatible. The listing sits at $25 to $50.

Third place fits because it addresses the case the others cannot. Frameless and ultra-thin bezel monitors give a conventional filter nothing to hold, and a hidden magnet design is built to attach without covering the picture edge. It also costs less than the standard pairs. The reason it is not first is that frameless fit is harder to guarantee, and the listing does not describe how the magnets anchor.

Buy it if you own a modern thin-bezel 24 inch monitor and standard hanging filters do not fit. Read the mounting instructions carefully before use.
pros: Hidden magnets keep a clean edge
products.idealFor: Buyers with a frameless monitor who need a magnetic mount built for that case.
products.skipIf: Your monitor has a wide, flat bezel.

products.name: JEEETINTX Magnetic Computer Privacy Screen Filter 27 Inch
products.verdict: A single magnetic hanging filter for 27 inch, 16:9 monitors.
products.description:
The JEEETINTX is a single magnetic hanging privacy filter for 27 inch, 16:9 monitors. Expect to pay $50 to $100.

Fourth place is right because it serves one size and is sold singly. For a 27 inch screen, there are few magnetic options, and this is the one in the ranking. The price per filter is higher than the 24 inch pairs, which is normal for a larger piece of film. If you have two 27 inch monitors, you would buy two, doubling the cost.

Choose it for a single 27 inch screen in an open area. If your monitor is a different size, do not stretch the fit.
cons: Sold singly, not in a pair
products.idealFor: Buyers with a 27 inch monitor who want a magnetic option.
products.skipIf: You have two monitors and want a pair.

products.name: GUDTEKE Magnetic 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor (Single)
products.verdict: The GUDTEKE design in a single 24 inch filter at a lower price.
products.description:
This is a single magnetic hanging GUDTEKE privacy screen for a 24 inch, 16:9 monitor. It is priced at $25 to $50.

Fifth place is fair because the two-pack gives you a second filter for little more. With one monitor, though, this is the cheapest way to try a magnetic filter. The design matches the pair, so there is nothing to learn about fit that the larger listing does not tell you.

Buy it if you have one 24 inch monitor and want to spend as little as possible. If you have, or may have, a second screen, buy the two-pack.
products.idealFor: Buyers with a single monitor who want the GUDTEKE design without paying for two.

methodology.title: Mounting design
methodology.description: We compared magnetic hanging mounts and hidden magnetic designs, since the mount decides whether a filter is easy to remove.

methodology.title: Size and ratio fit
methodology.description: We matched each filter to its stated diagonal and aspect ratio, as a wrong fit leaves part of the picture uncovered.

methodology.title: Frameless compatibility
methodology.description: We gave credit to designs that work on thin-bezel monitors, where standard hanging filters have nothing to grip.

methodology.title: Pack size and value
methodology.description: We weighed pairs against single filters, as a pair is cheaper per screen on dual-monitor desks.

methodology.title: Listing clarity
methodology.description: We marked down listings that give little detail and rewarded those that state the size, ratio, pack and mount plainly.

whatMatters.detail: Magnetic filters use small magnets to cling to the front of the monitor or to a bezel strip, so they lift off without adhesive. The result is a filter you can remove for presentations. Check the listing for how the magnets anchor, since a bare bezel may need a metal strip.

A bezel is the plastic frame around the screen, and many modern monitors have almost none. A hanging filter needs some edge to hold on, so frameless panels need a hidden design made for them. Look at your own monitor's edge before choosing.

The diagonal size and the ratio, 16:9 for most modern monitors, must match the filter. A filter cut for 16:9 will not cover a taller 16:10 panel. Measure the visible screen and compare it to the listing.
A two-pack suits a dual-monitor desk and usually costs less per screen. A single filter makes sense for one monitor, or if you only want to trial the idea. Check the count in the listing.

A privacy filter darkens the screen from the side and absorbs some light head-on. Raise the monitor's brightness to compensate. If a listing states an angle, such as 30 degrees, that tells you how narrow the sweet spot is.

faq.q: Will a magnetic filter stay on a monitor with no bezel?
faq.a: Not a standard hanging one. Frameless monitors need a design built for them, such as the JEAPKA hidden magnetic pair. Check how the magnets are meant to anchor before you buy.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with magnetic filters?
faq.a: Buying without looking at the monitor's edge. A thin or curved bezel may give the magnets nothing to hold. Check your screen from the side first.

faq.q: Is a magnetic filter worth it over an adhesive one?
faq.a: It is if you remove the filter often. A magnetic mount comes off without residue, while adhesive types can mark the screen. If the filter stays on permanently, adhesive is fine and often cheaper.
Clean the screen, place the filter's top edge or magnets as the instructions show, and let it settle flat. Smooth out any air gaps from the center. Re-seat it if it sags.
Small magnets near the edge are generally not a concern for modern LCD or LED panels. Do not use strong magnets over the display itself. Check the monitor maker's guidance if you have doubts.

faq.q: How do I clean and store the filter?
faq.a: Wipe gently with a dry microfiber cloth, and use a slightly damp one for smudges. Store it flat in a sleeve to avoid scratches and bends. Avoid sprays and strong chemicals.

finalTake: The GUDTEKE 2Pack is the best magnetic monitor privacy screen for most people, covering a pair of 24 inch panels with a clean, removable mount. The JEAPKA pair is a worthwhile alternative, the JEAPKA hidden design suits thin-bezel monitors, and the JEEETINTX is the choice for a 27 inch screen. Always check your monitor's edge first.
